title: AI-enabled gas sensors for breath-based diagnostics: smart mask platforms toward personalized healthcare
content: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) with breath-based gas detection is paving the way for promising advances in noninvasive diagnostics at the point of care. Specific volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in exhaled human breath act as biomarkers of several diseases. However, accurate breath analysis remains challenging because VOC concentrations vary from parts per billion (ppb) to parts per million (ppm). Conventional gas sensors suffer from humidity interference, baseline drift, signal noise, poor selectivity and sensor variability. AI enables robust pattern recognition, feature extraction and classification with improved accuracy. This review discusses how machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and the Internet of Things (IoT) transform conventional gas sensors into intelligent breath-monitoring devices. We review face-mask integration strategies, including fibre embedded, directly fabricated, and externally attached modular designs for real-time monitoring. We further discuss sensing materials, device architecture, data acquisition systems, cloud and edge computing platforms and ML and DL algorithms for disease prediction and wearable deployment. We also examine commercialization challenges, including the lack of universally accepted VOC biomarkers, the limited clinically validated datasets, privacy, model interpretability, and regulatory requirements. Finally, we highlight future directions toward clinically reliable, AI-enabled wearable breath diagnostic systems for personalized healthcare.
